prompts.title: An improper integral, with the limit written out
prompts.prompt: Show that the integral converges and find its value. Use correct notation in every step.
checklist: Rewrites the integral as a limit: $\lim_{b \to \infty} \int_1^b \frac{2}{x^3}\,dx$
Antidifferentiates and evaluates at $b$ and 1 inside the limit: $1 - \frac{1}{b^2}$
Takes the limit as a separate step and concludes the integral converges to 1, with no arithmetic on $\infty$

earns.answer: $\int_1^{\infty} \frac{2}{x^3}\,dx = \lim_{b \to \infty} \int_1^b 2x^{-3}\,dx = \lim_{b \to \infty} \left[-\frac{1}{x^2}\right]_1^b = \lim_{b \to \infty} \left(1 - \frac{1}{b^2}\right) = 1$. The limit exists, so the integral converges, to 1.
earns.why: Every step keeps the limit in front until it is taken, and the answer says the integral converges because the limit is a finite number.

misses.why: The value is right, but it substitutes $\infty$ as if it were a number. Readers give the point only with limit notation carried through to the end.
